subject: propagation rules to var in function

messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: propagation rules to var in function
parts:
Hi!

I was wondering if in the following user-specified function call what the final type of variable c will be:

real foo(vector c) { do stuff.. return result; }

real bar(real a, real b) {
   return foo(rep_vector(a/b, 2));
}

So if a or b are var, then the argument to foo (the c) will be var. But what happens if a and b is data in my Stan program? Will in that case a/b be passed into foo as data?

I am asking because I always get nervous when writing these functions as I run the risk of increasing the ad stack a lot.

Thanks!

Best,
Sebastian

On Thursday, July 21, 2016 at 7:55:38 AM UTC-4, Sebastian Weber wrote:
I was wondering if in the following user-specified function call what the final type of variable c will be:

User-defined functions are templated in the C++ code (except for int) and there is a lot of type promotion. That is the main reason why expose_stan_functions() is so brittle since it has to rewrite everything to only accept doubles from R rather than vars.

Ben

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: propagation rules to var in function
parts:
If you're using the function within a Stan program, there is no over-promotion. All the functions are templated on each argument type.

expose_stan_functions() is an rstan function that will bring the Stan program's user-defined functions into the R environment. A call to one of those functions may involve type promotion, if I understand Ben's email, but using user-defined functions within Stan programs do not incur that cost.


Daniel

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: propagation rules to var in function
parts:
On Thursday, July 21, 2016 at 11:54:23 AM UTC-4, Sebastian Weber wrote:
Well, that is what I am asking, i.e. if in the example I gave the created temporary rep_vector(a/b, 2) will be of type data if a and b are data?

If both a and b are doubles, then yes that is what templates do. But a and b can be doubles without being declared in the data block (e.g. transformed data or generated quantities) and sometimes in the transformed parameters and model blocks if you do something like foo(1, 2) or if you are calling foo() from R.

Ben
